# Research Brief: TineyIC Notebook / Town-Hall Revamp

*Prepared 2026-07-12 to inform the PRD handed to GPT-5.6. Audience: architecture decision-maker. Every factual claim is tagged to a numbered source [S#]; where the research pass produced thin or no evidence, that is stated rather than padded.*

**Bottom line up front.** The single most consequential finding is an ipykernel 7.x regression [S11]: detached background async tasks are not scheduled while the kernel is idle, which is exactly the mechanism the current "background worker streams tokens" design relies on. Building the town hall as a foreground/inline-streamed notebook UI on **anywidget**, with Python-side widget state as the source of truth, resolves both this risk and the re-run-safety constraint. Debate quality hinges on treating sycophancy as a first-class failure mode, not a nice-to-have.

---

## 1. Notebook UI Technology

### (a) What the evidence says

State-of-the-art custom notebook UI converges on **anywidget**. It runs across Jupyter, JupyterLab, Google Colab, VS Code, and marimo from a single widget definition [S3], because the browser loads one ES module directly from the kernel [S6]. It is a deliberately minimal layer over ipywidgets/traitlets that invents no new protocol [S4]; its widgets subclass ipywidgets and interoperate with core widgets [S6]. You install `pip install "anywidget[dev]"`, subclass `anywidget.AnyWidget`, and supply an ESM front end (inline `_esm`/`_css` or file paths) that exports a `render` (and optional `initialize`) hook [S3]. `render` runs exactly once per output cell; `initialize` runs once per instance [S4]. State syncs both ways via `traitlets(sync=True)`, with JS using `model.get/set/save_changes/on` regardless of which side originates the change [S3][S4]; the underlying transport is a per-object `BaseComm` implementing the Jupyter Widgets Message Protocol [S5][S6]. Beyond state sync, a separate custom-message channel (`widget.send({...})` → `model.on("msg:custom", cb)`) carries event-driven deltas — but messages are dropped if the widget has not been displayed yet [S4]. Binary data is serialized without base64 (`bytes`↔`DataView`), keeping high-frequency updates cheap [S4][S6]. HMR is opt-in via `ANYWIDGET_HMR=1` and updates the live view without re-executing cells [S3][S6]. Front ends may be vanilla JS or React/Svelte [S8]. An experimental `MimeBundleDescriptor`/`@widget` path can two-way-bind a plain dataclass/pydantic/msgspec/traitlets/psygnal object without subclassing `Widget`, but it is explicitly labeled unstable and "subject to change" [S5].

Jupyter Widgets generally provide two-way kernel↔front-end comms that static HTML outputs cannot match [S6]. The main alternatives:

- **Panel ChatFeed** runs in Jupyter and standalone, streams token-by-token via async generators ("the easiest and most optimal way") or a manual `stream()` that appends or replaces a message in place [S9]; a message can hold any object Panel can display plus custom `renderers` [S9]; it exposes imperative `send/stream/respond/stop/clear/undo/scroll_to/trigger_post_hook` and async callbacks [S9]; it is Panel v1.9.3 on Bokeh/Param and needs Pygments [S9].
- **Solara** is pure-Python React-style (on Reacton); the same code runs inline in Jupyter and as a standalone FastAPI/Starlette app, module-level `solara.reactive()` vars auto-re-render, latest is 1.60.3 with `requires_python >=3.8` (fine for 3.12), MIT-licensed, ~2.2k stars, with hot reload and Lab/Notebook/Voila/Colab/DataBricks/Datalore support [S12].
- **marimo** is a reactive notebook whose execution order is a DAG, not page order [S7]; deleting a cell removes its globals and re-runs dependents [S7]; every global must be defined by exactly one cell (underscore = cell-local) [S7]; a lazy runtime marks dependents stale instead of running them, positioned for expensive notebooks [S7][S8]; it is standardizing its plugin API on anywidget [S8] and ships 20+ built-in widgets plus a WASM playground [S8]. Critical caveat: marimo reasons only by static analysis and **does not track in-place mutations or attribute assignments** [S7].
- **ipywidgets async**: pausing a cell for interaction needs ipykernel 4.7+ and `%gui asyncio` [S10]; the canonical `wait_for_change` `asyncio.Future` helper (and a generator `yield_for_change` fallback) blocks a cell until a widget attribute changes [S10]; continuous background updates come from a `threading.Thread` mutating a displayed trait, not re-displaying it, with `unobserve` cleanup a required discipline [S10].

**The critical risk — ipykernel 7.x [S11].** On ipykernel 7.x (tested 7.1.0), background asyncio tasks (`create_task`/`ensure_future`) are not scheduled while the kernel is idle; side effects (even file writes) do not occur until another cell runs [S11]. It is a general async-scheduling regression, not a widget bug [S11]; the `set_parent()` workaround does not fix it, and the issue is open with no fix [S11]. It does not reproduce under JupyterLite (Pyodide/Xeus) [S11]. The exact broken idiom is the canonical live-UI pattern: `Button.on_click` → `asyncio.Queue` → long-lived background consumer → `Output` [S11]. Root cause is attributed to ipykernel PR #1451 with tracking issue ipython/ipykernel#1510 (referenced Mar 12, 2026); downgrading to ipykernel 6.x (6.31.0/6.3.1) restores immediate scheduling [S11].

### (b) What it means for TineyIC

The current app polls a Streamlit background worker; the wire already streams but output is collected before display. The revamp's entire premise — watch each persona think and write in real time — is the precise pattern [S11] breaks if implemented as a detached background task on modern ipykernel. This dominates the architecture. anywidget is the best-fit custom-UI layer: Python-first, uv-installable, single ESM, runs on every host the PRD names, thin over ipywidgets, with a custom-message channel that is the right token-streaming transport [S3][S4][S6]. Keeping authoritative state (transcript, per-turn `cognitive_state`, scorecard) in Python-side traitlets means a re-run or re-displayed widget rehydrates instead of losing history — directly serving "cell re-execution must be safe" and sidestepping the process-global registry crash by making the widget model the state owner [S4][S5].

### (c) Recommendation

Adopt **anywidget** as the town-hall render layer: one `AnyWidget` subclass owning transcript + `cognitive_state` as traitlets, an ESM front end with `render`/`initialize`, and token deltas pushed via the custom-message channel — displaying the widget *before* the debate loop emits, or early tokens are lost [S3][S4]. **Drive streaming from the foreground** (the executing cell), updating traits/Output as inline LLM chunks arrive, rather than a detached background task; if a background task is unavoidable, pin/test ipykernel 6.x (6.31.0 verified) and track #1510, and do not rely on `set_parent()` [S11]. Hold **Panel ChatFeed** as a fast-path fallback if a chat-feed metaphor suffices and the team accepts the Bokeh/Param/Pygments stack [S9]. Evaluate **marimo** as host for re-run safety only if streaming flows through marimo primitives (`mo.ui`, generators) rather than mutating shared objects, since it will not redraw on in-place mutation [S7][S8]. Target the stable `AnyWidget`+traitlets base; treat the experimental `@widget`/`MimeBundleDescriptor` path as optional ergonomics [S5].

## 2. Agent UX

### (a) What the evidence says

Upstream TinyTroupe displays agent output (including `[THOUGHT]`) as post-execution notebook output; no token-streaming or real-time thinking display is documented [S1]. It does ship an `AgentChatJupyterWidget` (ipywidgets) with a dropdown to pick an agent and send messages [S1], and an `Intervention` abstraction for event-based mid-run modifications [S1].

**assistant-ui** (React/TS) models a reasoning model as a typed sequence of parts — reasoning / tool-call / text [S14] — with compound components (`ReasoningRoot/Trigger/Content/Text`) that render reasoning separately from the answer [S14], groups consecutive reasoning+tool parts into one collapsible accordion via `GroupedParts` maintained during streaming [S14], and surfaces live state through `streaming`/`aria-busy` booleans driving a "thinking" indicator (no documented duration timer or auto-collapse) [S14]. It is React/TS-only with no Python; backend streaming is via the Vercel AI SDK [S14].

**Correction to flag (misconception in circulation):** it is *not* true that a non-standard runtime like LangGraph needs custom data parts (`makeAssistantDataUI`) merely to surface its reasoning. As of 2026-07-12 the official `@assistant-ui/react-langgraph` adapter converts LangGraph/LangChain reasoning/thinking blocks into the standard `{ type: "reasoning", text }` part rendered natively (a June 2026 fix hardened this) [S14]. What remains true: LangGraph does not stream reasoning in the AI SDK's built-in format, so assistant-ui's *automatic* chain-of-thought grouping does not auto-activate; `makeAssistantDataUI` is an optional path, not a requirement [S14].

**Virtual Roundtable** [S13] splits cognition into three visibility layers — private thoughts (hidden from other agents), public comments (shared), public ideas (proposals) [S13] — and has every thought/comment cite the prior entities that shaped it, enabling full lineage reconstruction rendered as a directed citation graph color-coded by source type (Fig. 9) [S13]. **TradingAgents** derives explainability from a full per-day log of each agent's reasoning, tool use, and thought processes under ReAct over shared state [S2]. For live updates, ipywidgets sanctions a background thread mutating a trait for continuous output and an `asyncio.Future` to await interaction [S10] — but the `Button`→`Queue`→background-consumer→`Output` idiom is exactly what breaks on ipykernel 7.x [S11]. In marimo, widgets are 2-way bindings read via plain `.value` with no callbacks, and `mo.stop` conditionally halts a cell [S8].

**Thin-evidence flag:** the angle also named AutoGen Studio, LangGraph Studio, CrewAI/ChatDev visualizers, Smallville/AI Town, and timeline scrubbing. This pass surfaced verifiable claims only for Virtual Roundtable [S13], TradingAgents [S2], assistant-ui [S14], and TinyTroupe [S1]. There is **no verified evidence** here on the spatial town-hall/Smallville metaphor or replay-scrubbing specifics — treat those as design exploration, not evidence-backed decisions.

### (b) What it means for TineyIC

Making THINK/`cognitive_state` first-class visible material is net-new: upstream gives none of it as live UI [S1]. Two precedents map cleanly. assistant-ui's typed-parts + collapsible reasoning-vs-answer pattern is the right *interaction* model — borrow the pattern, not the stack, since it cannot run in a kernel [S14]. Virtual Roundtable's private/public/proposal layering plus citation-lineage graph is a near-perfect fit for six investors: dimmed private THINK, public TALK, formal votes/memo, with disagreement analysis as an influence graph [S13]. `AgentChatJupyterWidget` is turn-based chat, not a streaming theater, so it is a base for the steering/input surface rather than the core render [S1]; `Intervention` is the native hook for user steering and devil's-advocate injection [S1].

### (c) Recommendation

Model each persona turn as typed streamable parts (think / talk / vote), mirroring assistant-ui, with a running-vs-complete indicator, and render THINK + `cognitive_state` as a collapsible reasoning block grouped with that persona's TALK [S14]. Adopt a **three-lane visibility model** — dimmed private thoughts (THINK + `cognitive_state`), public comment (TALK), formal proposal (votes/memo) [S13]. Require each utterance to cite the prior turns that shaped it so disagreement analysis renders as a first-class lineage graph [S13]. Implement user steering and the devil's advocate as facilitator-style interventions injected into the target persona's next prompt via TinyTroupe `Intervention` [S1][S13]. Build the bridge from TinyTroupe agent events to typed UI parts explicitly — the runtime won't emit standard reasoning parts, and (per the corrected LangGraph lesson) the right fix is an adapter that maps native events into a standard part type, not a pile of bespoke widgets [S14].

## 3. TinyTroupe (the substrate)

### (a) What the evidence says

Upstream is at **Release 0.7.0** (2026-03-28, adds vision), default model `gpt-5-mini` (legacy `gpt-4.1-mini`), Python 3.10+, **MIT-licensed** [S1] — so the project's vendored v0.6.0 fork trails upstream [S1]. It has a simulation control/checkpoint API — `control.begin("<name>.cache.json")` records, `control.checkpoint()` saves, `control.end()` terminates — plus LLM API caching that keeps every call in a map for cheaper, deterministic re-runs [S1]. It provides `ResultsExtractor`/`ResultsReducer` to turn interactions into structured outputs, `TinyPersonFactory` for persona generation, and a `SimulationExperimentEmpiricalValidator` for statistical comparison to real data [S1]. It ships `AgentChatJupyterWidget` (ipywidgets) and the `Intervention` hook [S1]. Its output is post-execution with no thinking stream [S1].

**Note on the registry crash:** the process-global agent/environment name-registry crash on re-run is stated in the project context, but this research pass did not surface any upstream issue or discussion confirming or fixing that specific behavior. Treat it as a local defect to own — there is no evidence of an upstream remedy to lean on.

### (b) What it means for TineyIC

Much of the revamp's plumbing already exists upstream and should be reused, not rebuilt: checkpoint/caching for safe re-execution and pause-between-phases, `Intervention` for steering, and `ResultsExtractor`/`ResultsReducer` for the vote scorecard and memo instead of hand-rolled extraction [S1]. The 0.6.0→0.7.0 gap matters (default model moved to `gpt-5-mini`; the project's 3.12 already satisfies 3.10+), and MIT licensing leaves the fork unencumbered [S1]. But the streaming-of-THINK centerpiece is not upstream and must be owned locally [S1], and the registry crash has no upstream shortcut evident.

### (c) Recommendation

Reuse before rebuild: extend `AgentChatJupyterWidget` for steering input; use `control.begin/checkpoint/end` + LLM caching to make phases pausable and cells re-runnable deterministically; generate the scorecard and memo via `ResultsExtractor`/`ResultsReducer` [S1]. Scope a migration path from the vendored 0.6.0 fork toward 0.7.0 conventions in the PRD, even if deferred [S1]. Own the streaming layer locally — tap the already-streaming wire and push deltas into per-persona panes, since collect-before-display is both the app's and upstream's default [S1]. Fix the process-global name registry as a first-class task (make the widget/model the state owner, fresh comm per re-run), with no upstream fix to rely on [S1][S5].

## 4. Prior Art & Competition

### (a) What the evidence says

The best-documented comparable is **TradingAgents** [S2]: seven LLM roles in a simulated firm (Fundamentals/Sentiment/News/Technical Analyst, Researcher, Trader, Risk Manager) in a fixed pipeline — a 4-analyst team → bull + bear researchers → a Trader → a 3-perspective Risk team → a Fund Manager who executes [S2]. It routes across two model tiers: quick-thinking (`gpt-4o-mini`/`gpt-4o`) for summarize/retrieve, deep-thinking (`o1-preview`) for reasoning/decisions, on API credits with no GPU [S2]. A 3-month backtest (Jan–Mar 2024; AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN) reports ≥23.21% cumulative / 24.90% annual, beating the best baseline by ~6.1%, with authors caveating an unusually high Sharpe and a short window forced by cost — ~11 LLM + 20+ tool calls per prediction [S2].

**Virtual Roundtable** is event-driven: four abstractions (Personas/Entities/Signals/Facilitator) communicate only through a central Event Bus, where every discourse action is published as an event rather than agents calling each other directly [S13]. On ecosystem reach, the anywidget front-end module standard is being adopted as marimo's plugin API, and Voila/Panel/Shiny-for-Python/Solara all support Jupyter Widgets, so anywidgets embed in standalone web apps too [S6].

**Thin-evidence flag:** the angle named virattt/ai-hedge-fund, FinRobot, and FinGPT. This pass produced **no verified claims** on those — only TradingAgents [S2] is deeply sourced. Popularity signals, form factors, and feature gaps for ai-hedge-fund/FinRobot/FinGPT were not established here and need a dedicated pass before the PRD leans on them.

### (b) What it means for TineyIC

TradingAgents is the strongest architectural template even though it is a trading pipeline, not a value-investor debate: its role specialization + facilitator + fund-manager execution and its tiered routing transfer directly [S2]. Its cost profile (~11 LLM + 20+ tool calls per decision) is a warning — a 6-persona × 4-phase debate will be LLM-expensive, so caching [S1] and tiered routing [S2] are levers, not niceties. Virtual Roundtable's Event Bus is a clean way to make streaming display and safe re-run both read from an append-only event stream instead of shared mutable agent state [S13].

### (c) Recommendation

Borrow TradingAgents' structure: specialized personas plus an explicit facilitator/fund-manager that gates phases and records structured verdicts [S2]. Adopt tiered model routing (cheap for summarize/retrieve, strong for THINK/verdict) against the OpenAI-compatible backend to control call volume [S2], and lean on TinyTroupe LLM caching for re-runs [S1]. Architect around an append-only, Event-Bus-style event stream so the town-hall render and re-execution both replay from events, not mutated state [S13]. Before the PRD makes competitive claims, commission a focused prior-art pass on ai-hedge-fund/FinRobot/FinGPT — not covered by this research.

## 5. Debate Method & Deliberation Quality

### (a) What the evidence says

**Sycophancy is the headline risk.** Inter-agent sycophancy causes premature "disagreement collapse" and yields *lower* accuracy than a single agent (CommonsenseQA: 85.50% single vs 83.62% two-agent debate) [S15]. Debater sycophancy correlates r=0.902 with agents abandoning their own correct answers to align with wrong peers (Negative Agreement Rate) [S15]. It intensifies in later rounds, so the paper recommends capping at 2–3 exchanges [S15]. It recommends composing debates from *mixed* roles — a high-sycophancy "peacemaker" (λ=8) plus a low-sycophancy "troublemaker" (λ=1) — rather than uniform sycophancy [S15]. Centralized (judge) frameworks are more resilient than decentralized ones, and judge sycophancy barely affects performance, so effort should go to debater composition, not judge tuning [S15]. It introduces three operational metrics: Disagreement Collapse Rate, Negative Agreement Rate, and a 0–100 Sycophancy Score [S15].

On protocol, **TradingAgents** runs bull-vs-bear for *n* rounds set by a debate facilitator, who then reviews the history, selects the prevailing perspective, and records it as a structured entry; the Risk team similarly debates three fixed stances under a facilitator before the Fund Manager finalizes [S2]. It uses a hybrid communication protocol (from MetaGPT): agents exchange concise structured reports queried from shared global state and use free-form NL *only* during agent-to-agent debate — an explicit fix for the "telephone effect" where long NL histories lose or distort earlier information [S2]. **Virtual Roundtable** runs a turn-based loop across a divergent (generate) then convergent (evaluate/rank) phase — one persona posts a public comment, then all others generate private thoughts before the next speaker [S13] — with a restraint-first facilitator whose interventions are embedded as age-marked context in targets' future prompts and a three-tier speaker-selection priority [S13]. Across 34 sessions (0–25 min), reasoning depth rose strongly with time (Influence Depth 10.8→70.7, r=0.79; Cross-Persona Absorption 0→83%, r=0.88) but idea diversity stayed flat (r=0.16, n.s.) — diversity is bounded by the personas present [S13].

### (b) What it means for TineyIC

Six value investors debating one stock sits squarely in the failure mode the sycophancy paper documents — they can collapse into agreement and score worse than one persona [S15]. The existing devil's advocate in cross-examination is validated as the needed "troublemaker" — keep and strengthen it [S15]. Longer debate buys *depth, not diversity* [S13], so breadth must come from the six distinct persona mandates plus the devil's-advocate phase, and extra rounds should go to convergence/rebuttal depth rather than open-ended chatter (which also feeds sycophancy) [S13][S15]. The final vote scorecard functions like the resilient centralized judge, so dissent-diversity belongs in the six debaters, not the judge [S15]. TradingAgents' structured-state + NL-only-in-debate split is the antidote to TinyTroupe's long-context telephone degradation and gives cells clean, re-renderable structured artifacts [S2].

### (c) Recommendation

Cap rebuttal/cross-examination at 2–3 exchanges and keep the final verdict tight [S15]. Engineer mixed temperaments across the six personas (some conciliatory, at least one hard dissenter per phase prompted to prioritize accuracy over agreement) rather than letting all six drift sycophantic [S15]. Persist opening statements, verdicts, and memo as structured records queried from shared TinyWorld state; reserve free-form streaming dialogue for cross-examination and rebuttal only [S2]. Add an explicit facilitator/"debate manager" that reads history, selects and records the structured verdict, gates phase transitions, and is the natural injection point for user steering [S2][S13] — kept restraint-first [S13]. Compute DCR/NAR-style disagreement metrics to power the disagreement-analysis output, and surface a Negative-Agreement moment in the THINK stream when a persona abandons an earlier contrarian stance [S15]. Optionally surface a depth/absorption signal so users see reasoning deepening even where diversity is bounded [S13].

## Recommendations Summary

| Decision | Recommendation | Confidence | Key sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custom UI layer | anywidget (single ESM over ipywidgets); Python-side traitlets own state | High | S3, S4, S6 |
| Streaming drive model | Foreground/inline cell streaming; avoid detached background tasks | High | S11, S10 |
| ipykernel version | Pin/test ipykernel 6.x or design around #1510; don't trust `set_parent()` | High (verified repro); upstream fix pending | S11 |
| Re-run safety | Widget model owns authoritative state; fresh widget+comm per run | High | S4, S5 |
| Fast-path fallback UI | Panel ChatFeed (token streaming, stop/undo) if a chat metaphor suffices | Medium | S9 |
| Reactive host option | Consider marimo, but route streaming via marimo primitives (no mutation reactivity) | Medium | S7, S8 |
| Reuse vs rebuild | checkpoint/caching + Intervention + ResultsExtractor/Reducer; migrate toward 0.7.0 | High | S1 |
| THINK visibility | Typed parts + three-lane private/public/proposal; collapsible reasoning block | High | S13, S14 |
| Disagreement analysis | Citation-lineage graph + DCR/NAR-style metrics | Medium | S13, S15 |
| Debate protocol | Structured-state + NL-only-in-debate; explicit facilitator/judge role | High | S2, S13 |
| Anti-sycophancy | Cap 2–3 rounds; mixed peacemaker/troublemaker; keep devil's advocate | High | S15 |
| Model cost control | Tiered quick/deep routing + LLM caching | Medium | S2, S1 |
| Town-hall metaphor / replay UX | Spatial Smallville-style + timeline scrubbing = design exploration; evidence thin | Low (gap) | — |

## Open Questions the PRD Must Settle

- **ipykernel target.** Pin 6.x for guaranteed background scheduling, or commit to a fully foreground/inline streaming design that is immune to ipython/ipykernel#1510? [S11]
- **Inline-await behavior.** Does cell-scoped `await wait_for_change` also suffer on ipykernel 7.x, or only detached tasks? The repro concerns idle-kernel background tasks; the inline-await case needs its own verification before choosing the pause/steer mechanism [S10][S11].
- **Host commitment.** Plain Jupyter (+anywidget) vs marimo. marimo solves re-run lifecycle but forbids define-in-one-cell/mutate-in-another and won't react to in-place mutation — is TineyIC willing to restructure agents/world into one-definition-plus-reset? [S7][S8]
- **Streaming transport.** Token-by-token anywidget custom messages vs frequent trait `save_changes` — the latency/throughput tradeoff is not settled by the docs and should be benchmarked [S3][S4].
- **Registry-crash fix.** This is a local defect with no upstream remedy found — confirm whether making the widget model the state owner fully resolves re-run crashes, or whether TinyTroupe internals still hold global name state [S1][S5].
- **Steering ownership.** TinyTroupe `Intervention` vs a custom facilitator-injection scheme — which owns user questions and devil's-advocate injection? [S1][S13]
- **Cost envelope.** With ~11 LLM + 20+ tool calls per decision as a reference point, what per-debate call/latency budget is acceptable for 6 personas × 4 phases, and how aggressively should the system cache and tier? [S2][S1]
- **Competitive scope.** ai-hedge-fund/FinRobot/FinGPT were not verified in this pass — does the PRD need a dedicated prior-art pass to position TineyIC? (research gap)
- **Fork currency.** How much of 0.7.0 to adopt now vs later, given the default-model change and a vision modality the project does not need? [S1]
